verses.1:1: And it happened, after Israel was taken captive and Jerusalem was laid waste, that Jeremiah sat weeping, and he lamented this lament over Jerusalem and said: Aleph. "How has she sat alone, the city that abounded with peoples? She has become like a widow, she who abounded among the nations; a ruler among the provinces, she has become subject to tribute.
verses.1:2: Beth. Weeping, she wept in the night, and her tears are on her cheeks, and there is no one who comforts her from among all those who love her; all those who cherish her have broken faith with her; they have become enemies to her.
verses.1:3: Gimel. Judea was deported because of her humiliation and because of the abundance of her servitude; she sat among the nations, she found no rest; all those pursuing her overtook her in the midst of those who afflict.
verses.1:4: Daleth. The roads of Zion mourn because there are none coming at the festival; all her gates are desolate, her priests groan, her virgins are being led away, and she herself is embittered within herself.
verses.1:5: He. Those who afflict her have become the head, and her enemies prospered, because the Lord humiliated her on account of the multitude of her impieties; her infants went into captivity before the face of one who afflicts.
verses.1:6: Waw. And all her splendor was taken away from the daughter of Zion; her rulers became like rams not finding pasture, and they went without strength before the face of one who pursues.
verses.1:7: Zayin. Jerusalem remembered the days of her humiliation and of her rejections, all her desirable things, as many as existed from ancient days, when her people fell into the hands of one who afflicts, and there was no one who helped her. Her enemies saw and laughed at her dwelling.
verses.1:8: Heth. Jerusalem sinned a sin; therefore she became an object of shaking; all those who honored her humiliated her, for they saw her indecency; and indeed she herself groans and has turned backward.
verses.1:9: Teth. Her uncleanness is at her feet; she did not remember her end, and she brought down extravagant things; there is no one who comforts her. See, Lord, my humiliation, for an enemy has magnified himself.
verses.1:10: Yod. One who afflicts stretched out his hand over all her desirable things; for she saw nations enter into her sanctuary, whom You commanded not to enter into Your assembly.
verses.1:11: Kaph. All her people are groaning, seeking bread; they gave her desirable things for food to restore life. See, Lord, and look, for she has become dishonored.
verses.1:12: Lamed. To you, all who pass along the way, turn and see if there is pain like my pain that has come about; having spoken against me, the Lord humiliated me in the day of the anger of His fury.
verses.1:13: Mem. From His height He sent fire; into my bones He brought it down; He spread out a net for my feet; He turned me backward; He made me desolate, in pain all the day.
verses.1:14: Nun. Watch was kept over my impieties; in my hands they were intertwined; they went up onto my neck; my strength grew weak, for the Lord put pains into my hands; I will not be able to stand.
verses.1:15: Samekh. The Lord removed all my strong ones from my midst; He summoned an appointed time against me to crush my chosen ones; the Lord trod a winepress for the virgin daughter of Judah; over these things I weep.
verses.1:16: Ayin. My eye has brought down water, for the one who comforts me is far removed from me, the one who restores my life; my sons have become desolate, for the enemy has prevailed.
verses.1:17: Pe. Zion spread out her hands; there is no one who comforts her. The Lord gave a command to Jacob: all around him are those who afflict him; Jerusalem has become a menstruating woman in their midst.
verses.1:18: Tsade. The Lord is righteous, for I embittered His mouth. Hear now, all you peoples, and see my pain: my virgins and my young men have gone into captivity.
verses.1:19: Qoph. I called to my lovers, but they deceived me; my priests and my elders expired in the city, for they sought food for themselves so that they might restore their lives, and they found none.
verses.1:20: Resh. See, Lord, that I am afflicted; my belly has been troubled, and my heart has been overturned within me; for embittering, I have been embittered; outside, a sword has bereaved, like death in the house.
verses.1:21: Shin. Hear now that I groan; there is no one who comforts me; all my enemies heard of my calamities and rejoiced, because You have done it; You brought on a day, You summoned an appointed time, they became like me.
verses.1:22: Taw. May all their wickedness come before Your face, and glean them in the way they made a gleaning on account of all my sins, for many are my groanings, and my heart is grieved."
verses.2:1: Aleph. How the Lord has darkened the daughter of Zion in His anger! He has cast down from heaven to earth the glory of Israel, and He has not remembered the footstool of His feet.
verses.2:2: Beth. In the day of His anger the Lord engulfed, not sparing; all the beautiful things of Jacob He tore down in His fury; the strongholds of the daughter of Judah He pressed to the ground; He profaned her kings and her rulers.
verses.2:3: Gimel. He called together in the anger of His fury every horn of Israel; He turned back His right hand from the face of an enemy, and He kindled in Jacob a flame like fire, and it devoured everything all around.
verses.2:4: Daleth. He bent His bow like a hostile enemy; He steadied His right hand like an adversary, and He killed all the desirable things of my eyes in the tent of the daughter of Zion; He poured out His fury like fire.
verses.2:5: He. The Lord has become like an enemy; He has engulfed Israel; He has engulfed her citadels; He has destroyed his strongholds, and He has multiplied for the daughter of Judah one being humiliated and one who has been humiliated.
verses.2:6: Waw. And He spread out His tabernacle like a vine; He destroyed His festival; the Lord forgot what He made in Zion of festival and Sabbath, and He provoked in the indignation of His anger king and priest and ruler.
verses.2:7: Zayin. The Lord has rejected His altar; He has shaken off His sanctuary; He has crushed in His hand the wall of her citadels; they gave voice in the house as on a day of festival.
verses.2:8: Heth. And He turned to destroy the wall of the daughter of Zion; He stretched out a measure; He did not turn back His hand from trampling; and the outer wall mourned, and the wall grew weak together.
verses.2:9: Teth. Her gates have sunk into the ground; He has destroyed and crushed her bars, her king and her rulers among the nations; there is no law, and indeed her prophets saw no vision from the Lord.
verses.2:10: Yod. The elders of the daughter of Zion sat on the ground, they kept silent; they cast up dust onto their heads; they wrapped themselves with sackcloth; they brought down to the ground the leading virgins in Jerusalem.
verses.2:11: Kaph. My eyes have failed with tears; my heart has been troubled; my glory has been poured out to the ground over the crushing of the daughter of my people, as infant and nursing child expire in the squares of the city.
verses.2:12: Lamed. To their mothers they said, "Where are grain and wine?" as they fainted like the wounded in the squares of the city, as their lives were poured out into the bosom of their mothers.
verses.2:13: Mem. What shall I testify to you, or to what shall I compare you, daughter of Jerusalem? Who will save and comfort you, virgin daughter of Zion? For the cup of your crushing has been magnified; who will heal you?
verses.2:14: Nun. Your prophets saw for you vain things and folly, and they did not uncover your injustice so as to turn back your captivity, and they saw for you vain pronouncements and expulsions.
verses.2:15: Samekh. All who pass along the way clapped their hands at you; they hissed and shook their heads at the daughter of Jerusalem: "This is the city," they will say, "the crown of gladness of all the earth."
verses.2:16: Ayin. All your enemies opened wide their mouths against you; they hissed and gnashed their teeth, and they said, "We have swallowed her up! Surely this is the day that we were expecting; we have found it, we have seen it."
verses.2:17: Pe. The Lord has done what He planned; He has accomplished His words that He commanded from ancient days; He tore down and did not spare, and He made an enemy glad over you; He exalted the horn of the one who afflicts you.
verses.2:18: Tsade. Their heart cried out to the Lord. Walls of Zion, bring down tears like torrents day and night; give yourself no respite; let not your eye keep silent, daughter.
verses.2:19: Qoph. Arise, exult in the night at the beginnings of your watch; pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord; lift up your hands to Him for the life of the infants who are fainting with hunger at the head of all the streets.
verses.2:20: Resh. See, Lord, and look at whom You have gleaned like this! Will women eat the fruit of their womb? A butcher has made a gleaning; will infants nursing at the breasts be murdered? Will You kill priest and prophet in the sanctuary of the Lord?
verses.2:21: Shin. Young boy and old man lay down in the street; my virgins and my young men went into captivity; by sword and by famine You killed; in the day of Your anger You butchered, You did not spare.
verses.2:22: Taw. He summoned a day of festival of my sojourning all around, and in the day of the Lord's anger there was no one escaping and no one left behind, as I overpowered and multiplied all my enemies.
verses.3:1: Aleph. I am the man who sees poverty; with the rod of His wrath against me,
verses.3:2: He took me and led me away into darkness and not light.
verses.3:3: Only against me He turned His hand all day long.
verses.3:4: He made my flesh and my skin grow old; He shattered my bones.
verses.3:5: Beth. He built up against me, and surrounded my head and toiled.
verses.3:6: In dark places He seated me, like the dead of old.
verses.3:7: He built up against me, and I will not go out; He made my bronze heavy.
verses.3:8: Gimel. And indeed I will cry out and shout; He has blocked off my prayer.
verses.3:9: Daleth. He walled up my ways; He blocked up my paths; He disrupted them.
verses.3:10: A bear lying in ambush, He is to me a lion in hidden places.
verses.3:11: He pursued one who had departed and stopped me; He made me desolate.
verses.3:12: He. He bent His bow and set me up like a target for an arrow.
verses.3:13: He brought the arrows of His quiver into my kidneys.
verses.3:14: I became a laughingstock to all my people, their song all day long.
verses.3:15: Waw. He filled me with bitterness; He made me drunk with gall.
verses.3:16: And He knocked out my teeth with gravel; He fed me ashes.
verses.3:17: And He thrust my soul away from peace; I forgot good things.
verses.3:18: And my victory and my hope from the Lord perished.
verses.3:19: Zayin. I remembered from my poverty and from persecution; my bitterness and gall will be remembered,
verses.3:20: and my soul will brood over me.
verses.3:21: This I will set in my heart; therefore I will wait.
verses.3:25: Heth. The Lord is good to those who wait for Him, to the soul that will seek Him as good;
verses.3:26: and it will wait and be quiet for the salvation of the Lord.
verses.3:27: Teth. It is good for a man when he lifts a yoke in his youth;
verses.3:28: he will sit alone and be silent, because he lifted it upon himself.
verses.3:30: Yod. He will give the cheek to the one who strikes him; he will be filled with reproaches,
verses.3:31: because the Lord will not forever reject.
verses.3:32: Kaph. For the One who humbled will have compassion, even according to the abundance of His mercy.
verses.3:33: He did not answer from His heart and humble the sons of man.
verses.3:34: Lamed. To humble all the prisoners of the earth under his feet,
verses.3:35: to turn aside the justice of a man before the face of the Most High,
verses.3:36: to condemn a person when he is being judged—the Lord did not speak.
verses.3:37: Who spoke in this way, and it came to be? The Lord did not command it.
verses.3:38: From the mouth of the Most High, will not evil things and good come out?
verses.3:39: Mem. Why should a living person grumble, a man concerning his sin?
verses.3:40: Nun. Our way has been searched out and examined, and let us return to the Lord;
verses.3:41: let us lift up our hearts upon our hands to the High One in heaven.
verses.3:42: We have sinned, we have acted impiously, and You have not pardoned.
verses.3:43: Samekh. You spread a covering in wrath and chased us away; You killed, You did not spare.
verses.3:44: You spread a cloud as a covering for Yourself because of prayer,
verses.3:45: so that I should close my eyes and be rejected. Ayin. You placed us in the midst of the peoples.
verses.3:46: All our enemies opened their mouth wide against us.
verses.3:47: Fear and wrath came upon us, lifting up and shattering.
verses.3:48: My eye will bring down streams of water over the shattering of the daughter of my people.
verses.3:49: Pe. My eye has been swallowed up, and I will not be silent, because there is no recovery,
verses.3:50: until the Lord peers down and sees from heaven.
verses.3:51: My eye will glean upon my soul more than all the daughters of the city.
verses.3:52: Tsade. Hunting, all my enemies hunted me like a sparrow without cause.
verses.3:53: They put my life to death in a pit and placed a stone upon me.
verses.3:54: Water poured over my head; I said, "I have been rejected."
verses.3:55: Qoph. I called upon Your name, Lord, from the lowest pit.
verses.3:56: You heard my voice; do not hide Your ears from my supplication.
verses.3:57: You drew near for my help; on the day I called upon You, You said to me, "Do not fear."
verses.3:58: Resh. You decided, Lord, the cases of my soul; You redeemed my life.
verses.3:59: You saw, Lord, my troubles; You judged my cause.
verses.3:60: You saw all their vengeance, into all their thoughts against me.
verses.3:61: Shin. You heard their reproach, all their thoughts against me,
verses.3:62: the lips of those who rise up against me and their meditations against me all day long,
verses.3:63: their sitting down and their rising up. Look upon their eyes;
verses.3:64: You will render to them a repayment, Lord, according to the works of their hands.
verses.3:65: Taw. You will render to them a shielding, hardship of heart.
verses.3:66: You will pursue them in anger and completely consume them beneath heaven, Lord.
verses.4:1: Aleph. How will gold grow dim, the good silver be altered? Holy stones were poured out at the head of all the streets.
verses.4:2: Beth. The precious sons of Zion, those lifted up in gold, how were they counted as earthenware vessels, works of a potter's hands?
verses.4:3: Gimel. Even dragons bared their breasts; their cubs nursed the daughters of my people to an incurable state, like a sparrow in a wilderness.
verses.4:4: Daleth. The tongue of a nursing infant clung to his throat in thirst. Little children asked for bread; there is no one who breaks it for them.
verses.4:5: He. Those who ate the foods were devastated in the streets; those who were reared upon scarlet clothed themselves in dunghills.
verses.4:6: Waw. And the iniquity of the daughter of my people became greater than the iniquities of Sodom, which was overthrown as in haste, and they did not weary their hands in her.
verses.4:7: Zayin. Her Nazirites were purer than snow, they shone more than milk, they were more fiery than stones, their fragment was of sapphire.
verses.4:8: Heth. Their appearance grew darker than soot; they were not recognized in the streets. Their skin was fixed upon their bones; they dried up, they became like wood.
verses.4:9: Teth. Better were those wounded by the sword than those wounded by famine; they departed pierced through, away from the produce of the fields.
verses.4:10: Yod. The hands of compassionate women boiled their children; they became food for them in the shattering of the daughter of my people.
verses.4:11: Kaph. The Lord completed His wrath; He poured out the wrath of His anger, and He kindled a fire in Zion, and it devoured her foundations.
verses.4:12: Lamed. The kings of the earth did not believe, all who inhabit the world, that an enemy and an oppressor would enter through the gates of Jerusalem.
verses.4:13: Mem. Because of the sins of her prophets, the injustices of her priests, those who shed righteous blood in her midst.
verses.4:14: Nun. Her watchers staggered in the streets; they were defiled with blood in their inability; they touched their garments.
verses.4:15: Samekh. Depart from the unclean; call to them, "Depart, depart, do not touch!" because they were kindled and even staggered. Say among the nations, "They will by no means sojourn any longer."
verses.4:16: Ayin. The face of the Lord is their portion; He will no longer look upon them. They did not regard the face of priests; they did not have mercy on prophets.
verses.4:17: Pe. While we still existed, our eyes failed, as we watched in vain for our help.
verses.4:18: Tsade. We watched for a nation that does not save; we hunted our little ones so as not to walk in our squares.
verses.4:19: Qoph. Our time has drawn near, our days have been fulfilled, our time is here. Those who pursue us became swifter than eagles of the sky; upon the mountains they flew forth, in a wilderness they lay in wait for us.
verses.4:20: Resh. The breath of our face, the anointed Lord, was captured in their destructions, of whom we said, "In his shadow we will live among the nations."
verses.4:21: Shin. Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Idumea, who dwells upon the earth; even to you the cup of the Lord will pass; you will become drunk and pour out.
verses.4:22: Taw. Your iniquity has come to an end, daughter of Zion; He will no longer carry you into exile. He has visited your iniquities, daughter of Edom; He has uncovered your ungodly deeds.
verses.5:1: Remember, Lord, what has happened to us; look and see our reproach.
verses.5:2: Our inheritance has been transferred to outsiders, our houses to foreigners.
verses.5:3: We have become orphans, there is no father; our mothers are like widows.
verses.5:4: From our days, our wood came at a price; upon our neck
verses.5:5: we were pursued; we grew weary, we were not given rest.
verses.5:6: Egypt gave a hand, Assyria, for their satisfaction.
verses.5:7: Our fathers sinned, they are no more; we have borne their lawless deeds.
verses.5:8: Servants have ruled over us; there is no redeemer from their hand.
verses.5:9: With our lives we will bring in our bread because of the sword of the wilderness.
verses.5:10: Our skin turned livid like an oven; they were shriveled up because of the storms of famine.
verses.5:11: They humiliated women in Zion, virgins in the cities of Judah.
verses.5:12: Rulers were hung by their hands; elders were not honored.
verses.5:13: Chosen men took up weeping, and young men grew weak under wood.
verses.5:14: And old men ceased from the gate; chosen men ceased from their songs.
verses.5:15: The joy of our heart has come to an end; our dance has been turned into mourning.
verses.5:16: The crown of our head has fallen. Woe now to us, for we have sinned.
verses.5:17: Because of this our heart has become a painful grief; because of this our eyes have grown dark.
verses.5:18: Over Mount Zion, because it has been devastated, foxes have passed through it.
verses.5:19: But You, Lord, will dwell forever; Your throne is to generation and generation.
verses.5:20: Why will You utterly forget us? Will You forsake us for length of days?
verses.5:21: Turn us back, Lord, to Yourself, and we will be turned back; and renew our days as before.
verses.5:22: For You have completely rejected us; You have become exceedingly angry with us.

notes.1:1: The Greek text opens with a narrative prologue attributing the lament to Jeremiah (not found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text) and retains the transliterated Hebrew alphabet acrostic headings throughout chapters 1-2.
notes.1:3: The Greek uses the proper name Judea (rather than Judah, as in 1:15) and renders the final phrase as "those who afflict," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "narrow straits."
notes.1:12: The Greek opens with the difficult phrasing "To you, all who pass..." and adds the participle "having spoken against me," differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("Is it nothing to you... which was dealt to me").
notes.1:14: Instead of the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "yoke of my transgressions... bound by His hand," the Greek reads "Watch was kept over my impieties; in my hands they were intertwined," and concludes "put pains into my hands."
notes.1:22: The Greek translates the Hebrew verb for dealing harshly as a vineyard-gleaning metaphor ("glean / gleaning," repeated in 2:20) and uses the third-person plural "they made" rather than the Masoretic Text's second-person singular.
notes.2:3: The Greek text reads "He called together" (synekalesen), a Greek textual variant for "He broke in pieces" (syneklasen), corresponding to the Hebrew "He cut off."
notes.2:10: The Greek reads "the leading virgins" (archegous parthenous) as the direct object of "they brought down," rendering the Hebrew word for "head" in its sense of "leader/chief."
notes.2:16: In the Greek text the acrostic headings of 2:16 (Ayin) and 2:17 (Pe) follow standard alphabetical order, even though the underlying Hebrew verses of chapter 2 place Pe (2:16) before Ayin (2:17).
notes.2:20: Continuing the gleaning metaphor of 1:22, the Greek adds "A butcher has made a gleaning" (linked to "You butchered" in 2:21) and includes the question "will infants nursing at the breasts be murdered?"
notes.2:22: The Greek closes the chapter with "as I overpowered and multiplied all my enemies," reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew than the Masoretic Text's "those whom I bore and reared, my enemy has destroyed."
notes.3:1: The Greek text preserves transliterated Hebrew acrostic letter names (such as Βή, Οὐαύ, Ζάι, and Λάβδ) placed at irregular stanza divisions rather than the Hebrew three-verse intervals. The phrase 'against me' (ἐπ᾽ ἐμέ) stands at the end of v. 1 in the Greek tradition, leading directly into v. 2.
notes.3:5: The Greek reads 'my head' (κεφαλήν μου) and the verb 'toiled' (ἐμόχθησεν), reflecting a different interpretation of the Hebrew words that the Masoretic Text reads as 'gall and hardship.'
notes.3:25: Verses 22–24 (as well as v. 29) are absent from this Greek witness, matching the Codex Vaticanus tradition. In addition, 'good' (ἀγαθόν) stands at the end of v. 25 ('seek Him as good') rather than opening v. 26 as in the Hebrew text and some Greek editions.
notes.3:33: The Greek reads 'answer' (ἀπεκρίθη), rendering the Hebrew verb root as 'answer' rather than its homonym 'afflict.'
notes.3:45: The Greek places the opening infinitives ('so that I should close my eyes and be rejected') before the acrostic heading Ayin, connecting them to v. 44 rather than reading 'offscouring and refuse' with 'You placed us' as in the Hebrew.
notes.3:51: The Greek verb ἐπιφυλλιεῖ literally means 'will glean,' reflecting a Hebrew verb that can mean both 'glean' and 'deal severely with.' The preposition παρά with the accusative may be read either as 'more than' or 'because of.'
notes.3:63: The Greek ends the verse with 'Look upon their eyes' (ἐπίβλεψον ἐπ᾽ ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν), differing from the Hebrew 'Look! I am their mocking song.'
notes.3:65: The Greek translates the Hebrew word for 'covering/dullness (of heart)' literally as 'shielding' (ὑπερασπισμόν) and joins 'of heart' with 'hardship' (καρδίας μόχθον).
notes.4:1: Each verse of chapter 4 opens in the Greek text with a transliterated Hebrew acrostic letter name, rendered here using standard English spellings. The Greek reads "the good silver" (to argyrion to agathon) with future passive verbs, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "fine gold."
notes.4:3: The Greek places "their cubs" in the nominative and "the daughters of my people" in the accusative as the object of "nursed," differing from the Hebrew clause division. Greek strouthion literally means "sparrow," though it renders a Hebrew word for ostriches.
notes.4:18: The Greek verse division places "We watched for a nation that does not save" at the start of 4:18 rather than in 4:17 (similarly shifting the opening of 4:19), and reads first-person "we hunted our little ones" where the Hebrew reads "they hunted our steps."
notes.4:20: The Greek reads nominative christos Kyrios ("the anointed Lord," rather than the Hebrew genitive "the Lord's anointed"); the pronoun autou ("his shadow") is lowercase here as referring to the captured Judean king, though traditional Christian exegesis reads the phrase messianically ("His shadow").
notes.4:21: The Greek uses the Hellenized name Idumea (Idoumaia) here while using Edom in 4:22, and reads "upon the earth" without naming Uz as in the Hebrew.
notes.5:4: The Greek omits the Hebrew clause about buying water for silver, beginning instead with "From our days" (ex hemeron hemon). The closing phrase "upon our neck" continues directly into the opening verb of 5:5 ("we were pursued").
notes.5:6: The Greek makes "Egypt" the subject of a third-person singular verb ("gave a hand") and omits "bread," which appears in the Hebrew.
notes.5:10: The Greek pairs a singular verb ("turned livid," epeliothe) with a plural verb ("they were shriveled up," synespasthesan) and reads "storms of famine" (kataigidon limou).
notes.5:13: The Greek reads "chosen men" (eklektoi, also in 5:14) and "took up weeping" (klauthmon anelabon), where the Hebrew refers to young men bearing the millstone.
notes.5:20: "Utterly" translates Greek eis nikos (literally "to victory"), an established Septuagint idiom meaning "completely" or "permanently."
